children: ValueAct Capital (“ValueAct”) today published a presentation outlining the case for its proposals ahead of the Extraordinary General Meeting of Takara Holdings Inc. (“Takara”, the “Company”) shareholders to be held on December 16, 2026. Funds managed by ValueAct own approximately 20% of the shares outstanding.
The presentation is available at
this link
Takara has strong brands but weak results
Takara owns strong brands with global growth potential, including Sho Chiku Bai sake, Blanton’s bourbon, and Tomatin scotch. Its results do not reflect that potential:
The medium-term plan that ended in March 2026 missed all financial targets. Operating profit was 55% below target.1
Return on equity fell to 4.6%, against the Company’s reported cost of equity of 7.4%.2
Total shareholder return trailed the TOPIX index by 54 percentage points in the five years before ValueAct’s investment was publicly disclosed.3

Takara is not realizing its potential as a result of the Board’s failure to fulfill each of its responsibilities as defined by METI and TSE4: (1) to develop a value-accretive strategy, (2) to allocate capital efficiently, (3) to provide independent oversight of M&A, and (4) to effectively supervise management.
The Outside Directors have failed to provide effective independent oversight

Japan’s Corporate Governance Code (Principle 4.8, Interpretive Guidance) calls on Outside Directors to protect the common interests of shareholders when business performance deteriorates and, where management has a conflict of interest, to make judgments themselves as decision makers. The failure of the Outside Directors to fulfill their responsibilities is apparent in three significant Board decisions:
Lack of independent oversight of the tender offer for Takara Bio, the Company’s largest-ever capital allocation decision.

The Board approved the ¥54.5 billion debt-funded tender offer without forming a committee of Takara Holdings’ Outside Directors and without disclosing any independent verification of management’s forecasts, despite the many management conflicts of interest apparent in this transaction. In the nine months since the Board approved the tender offer, accounting issues at Takara Bio USA have surfaced, and management’s forecasts have been revised down twice.
Approval of Medium-Term Management Plan 2030 (“MTMP 2030”), which repeats the failed Medium-Term Management Plan 2025 (“MTMP 2025”).

Despite the failure of MTMP 2025 to meet any of its financial targets and the fact that 91% of Takara’s invested capital now sits in businesses that do not earn more than the Company’s reported cost of capital,5 the Outside Directors did not require an independent review of Takara’s strategy and business portfolio before approving MTMP 2030 which pursues substantively the same strategy, creating significant risk of more missed targets and a continuation of Takara’s low return on invested capital.
Refusal to develop a President succession plan and refusal to implement a compensation system that pays for performance.

Takara is one of just 14% of Prime-listed companies that do not comply with Supplementary Principle 4.1.3 of the Corporate Governance Code on President succession planning,6 and one of just 7% of Prime-listed companies that do not have a long-term incentive plan.7
ValueAct asked the Outside Directors to act, but was declined

The Board has refused to engage with the substance of the issues that ValueAct has raised, including the Company’s deteriorating performance, unfocused strategy and business portfolio, lack of a President succession plan, and lack of key skillsets on the Board.

In February 2026 ValueAct asked for an independent review of strategy and the business portfolio, led by the Outside Directors. In July and September 2026 ValueAct asked the Board to allow the Outside Directors to engage on President succession and the composition of the Board. The Board declined each request, leaving ValueAct no option but to request a shareholder meeting.
Three Outside Directors should be held accountable

Three incumbent Outside Directors – Masako Tomotsune, Tomoko Kawakami, and Takao Motomiya – are responsible for Takara’s deteriorating performance and weak oversight during their tenures and are proposed to be removed. Ms. Tomotsune is Chair, and Ms. Kawakami and Mr. Motomiya are members, of the Nomination and Compensation Committee which has shown an inability to supervise management from an independent perspective.

These incumbent Outside Directors have, according to the Company’s own AGM notice, “never been involved in the management of a company except as an outside officer.” The Board’s own May 2026 effectiveness evaluation cites “ongoing challenges regarding the monitoring function of the Board of Directors.” ValueAct concludes that these incumbent Outside Directors do not possess the required skillset to adequately oversee the Takara Holdings business and management at this critical time for the Company.
Removal is the only way to add new directors

Takara lowered the maximum size of its Board from ten to seven in 2022, and all seven seats are filled. A vote FOR the nominees takes effect only if incumbents are removed. Without removals, there can be no change in the Board’s composition.
Three nominees with the skillset the Board requires

All three candidates nominated by ValueAct have been CEO or CFO of a listed company in Japan, have direct business experience relevant to Takara’s key industries, and have capital markets and capital allocation experience from the perspective of an operator. All are independent of ValueAct and Takara.
Eric Johnson
is the former Representative Director and CEO of JSR Corporation and the founder of JSR Life Sciences
Yuko Tashiro
is a former audit partner at KPMG, the former President of Accordia Golf and an Outside Director of McDonald’s Holdings Company (Japan)
Marc André Tousignant
is the former Global Chief Financial Officer of Suntory Global Spirits and chaired its Capital & Investment Committee
What the proposals accomplish

If all six proposals pass, the Board will remain at seven directors. Four will be independent Outside Directors, including Seiichiro Shirahata, who joined the Board in 2025. The three executive directors will continue. ValueAct is not seeking control of Takara or any specific strategy or transaction.

What changes is the Board’s capability. The proposals establish a Board capable of effectively overseeing strategy, capital allocation and management, and of contributing to the sustainable growth of the Company.
ValueAct recommends that shareholders vote:
FOR proposals 1-3
to remove Outside Directors Masako Tomotsune, Tomoko Kawakami and Takao Motomiya
FOR proposals 4-6
to elect Eric Johnson, Yuko Tashiro and Marc André Tousignant as independent Outside Directors
More information on ValueAct’s proposals is available at: www.treasuretakara.com.
About ValueAct Capital

ValueAct Capital, established in 2000, is a global investment firm managing capital on behalf of some of the world’s largest institutional investors. ValueAct seeks to identify and invest in high-quality businesses that are temporarily undervalued, taking a patient, collaborative and constructive approach to value-building for all stakeholders, often partnering with executives and board members. Since 2017, ValueAct has been a significant investor in the Japanese public equity markets. In the firm’s history, partners of ValueAct have served on over 55 public company board seats, including on the boards of two Japanese public companies.
